label: Q1b-i full mark: 'data about the data'
question: Q1b-i
answer: Data about the data stored in the file, such as dimensions and file size.
notes: Textbook accepted phrasing — 'data about data' plus concrete examples from the Accept list.

label: Q1b-i zero: 'information about the image' (rejected)
question: Q1b-i
notes: Mark scheme explicitly Do Not Accept — 'information about the image' without qualification is too vague.

label: Q1b-iii full mark: '16'
question: Q1b-iii
notes: Mark scheme accepts only the value 16.

label: Q1b-iii zero: common '4' error
question: Q1b-iii
notes: Flagged in the examiner report as a common error — confusing bits with number of colours.

label: Q1b-iv full mark: two distinct effects
question: Q1b-iv
answer: More colours can be represented, and the file size will increase because each pixel needs more bits to store.
notes: Two accepted effects: greater range of colours + larger file size.

label: Q1b-iv partial: one valid effect only
question: Q1b-iv
notes: Single accepted effect — no coverage of the second mark.

label: Q1b-iv zero: rejected phrasings
question: Q1b-iv
answer: The resolution will be better and the sound will be clearer.
notes: Both phrasings are on the Do Not Accept list — resolution relates to pixels not colour depth, sound relates to sampling.

label: Q1c-i full mark: lossless + two justifications
question: Q1c-i
answer: Lossless compression. No data is lost, so the text remains readable. If characters were removed the text would become corrupted.
notes: Correct type + two accepted justifications ('no data lost' and 'text would corrupt without characters').
